concise_summary: PKD develops a unified theodicy synthesizing Dante's three realms with Joachim of Fiore's three historical ages (Father-Machine, Son-Human, Spirit-Divine). He argues that Blade Runner footage confirmed his 2-3-74 vision as an ascent through Inferno (hell as mechanism and law), Purgatorio (time flowing backward), and Paradiso (God/VALIS revealed). The topology is theological: Christ's advent introduced choice and time to break machine-determinism, creating a "winnowing" of souls, but true salvation requires a third testament (glimpsed as the Plasmate) latent in the New Testament itself, accessible only through grace and a heroic inner act.
key_claims: The Logos perceived in PKD's vision is Greek-sourced and Judeo-Christian apocalyptic in frame, realizing Eckhart's fourth stage where the world pre-exists as abstract forms in God's intellect

Dante's three realms (Inferno, Purgatorio, Paradiso) are coaxial with Joachim's three ages and correspond to three levels of being: machine (ruled by Law), human (moral choice), and Ditheon (God-inscribed heart)

Christ's advent was paradoxically both successful (it introduced freedom, choice, and time) and failed (it did not usher in the age of the Spirit, only created a winnowing); Age 3 is still latent, awaiting an external revolutionary act

The Bible is a living, sentient organism that 'intrudes one-way from outside' and contains three hidden testaments: the Old Testament (Law/Inferno), New Testament (Choice/Purgatorio), and a Third Testament (Spirit/Paradiso) concealed as the Plasmate
Anamnesis (recovered memory) plus perception of coaxial hierarchy plus ascent plus temporal transformation constitute 'meta-abstraction'—the condition of seeing through multiple frames simultaneously

Satan represents pre-law chaos; the Law compels external good without saving the soul; Grace offers choice and the risk of damnation—the entire post-advent world is an extended eschatological judgment and wager on human freedom
